history.dynasty: None (Indian Army — Corps of Electrical and Mechanical Engineers)
history.summary: Built in February 1966 by the Indian Army's Corps of Electrical and Mechanical Engineers (EME) during the tenure of Brig AF Eugene, the first Commandant of the EME School, Vadodara — himself a Christian. The modern geodesic aluminium-dome temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva as Dakshinamurthy, the supreme teacher, and is a symbol of secularism: its kalasha (Hinduism), dome (Islam), tower (Christianity), golden finial (Buddhism), entrance (Jainism) and havan kund (Zoroastrianism) reflect India's major faiths. The landscaped campus holds 106 ancient statues dating from the 6th to the 16th century. In 2023, Maj Gen Neeraj Varshney added a Navgraha temple, a scale replica of the main shrine. The temple is run and maintained by Indian Army authorities.

name: EME Temple (Dakshinamurthy Temple)
town_description: Vadodara (formerly Baroda) is a major city in Gujarat on the Vishwamitri river, famed as the cultural capital of the state. It was the seat of the Gaekwad rulers, whose patronage left palaces, museums and temples across the city. The city hosts the EME School of the Indian Army and a large petrochemical industry.

travel.road: On EME Road / Mandir Marg, Fatehgunj; reachable by local buses and auto-rickshaws from anywhere in the city

visitor_information.best_time: October-March; Maha Shivratri and Janmashtami for the festival atmosphere
visitor_information.opening_hours: CONFLICT (verify): Wikipedia says 6:00 AM-9:00 PM daily (aarti 6:45 PM on Tuesdays); Gujarat Tourism lists 5:30 AM-8:00 PM; other sources 6:30 AM-8:30 PM, with Sunday open vs closed disputed. Valid photo ID required at entrance (army area). Photography rules disputed across sources - seek permission before photographing.
